title: Tujia language - Wikipedia
text: The Tujia language is a Sino-Tibetan language spoken natively by the Tujia people in Hunan Province, China. It is unclassified within the Sino-Tibetan language family, due to pervasive influence from neighboring languages.

title: Tujia Language – Knowledge.Deck.no
text: The Tujia language has several features that distinguish it from other Sino-Tibetan languages. It has a rich phonemic inventory, including a variety of tonal distinctions in the Southern dialect, which are absent in the Northern dialect.

title: Tujia - Sino-Tibetan Branches Project (STBP) by Andy Hsiu
text: Tujia is a an independent Sino-Tibetan branch consisting of two living languages, namely Northern Tujia ("Bitsi" / "Miji") and Southern Tujia ("Mongji"). It does not subgroup with any other Sino-Tibetan branch, pointing to its position as an early split from Sino-Tibetan.
